text.p: A Potlatch Corp executive forecast that the forest products company's depreciation and amortization next year will be $145 million to $150 million compared to $140 million to $145 million this year.

The executive, Sandy Powell, vice president for financial services, also forecast that capital expenditures net year would range from $175 million to $190 million compared to $250 million to $260 million in 1996.
Speaking at the Atlanta Society of Financial Analysts, Powell also forecast that deferred taxes in 1997 would be $20 million to $25 million, compared with $10 million to $15 million this year.
She said that the San Francisco-based company's gross interest expense in 1997 would be about $50 million to $51 million versus $53 million to $54 million this year.
Powell said that the company's capitalized interest next year would be about $6 million to $8 million compared to $10 million this year.
Powell added that the company's tax rate would be "no higher" than 34 percent this year and that it would probably rise to 37 percent in 1997.
